title: VQ normalization mismatch in the first matched logit pilot
tool: quantization_logit_run.py, quantization_logit_compare.py, audit-vq-norms-v1.py
---

The native affine baseline and both VQ arms completed all six owned contexts under their frozen supervision and memory limits. The full 4.4 artifact was verified and its four-layer traversal proof passed. These are execution/provenance results only. The resulting quality comparison is invalid: the two VQ arms shared a wrong normalization convention. Finite outputs, strict parameter loading and traversal equality did not detect it.

The pinned PR 1788 architecture applies non-gated norm weights directly. Its sanitizer adds one only when raw HF key prefixes occur. Both inspected VQ packs use converted model.* names while retaining raw zero-centered norms. The bounded direct-byte audit below verifies every one of the 148 affected tensors in each pack: none match the deployed baseline raw, and adding one with BF16 round-to-nearest-even makes all of them byte-identical. The gated delta-net norm already stores its scale and is excluded. The PR's own current description documents this convention incompatibility. No model or tokenizer file was modified.

The first pilot therefore cannot rank quality or support a candidate win. Both old traversal proofs and earlier full-reference feasibility outputs also omitted this fold. They prove bounded execution of that incorrect configuration, not semantic model correctness. Corrected execution must identify the adapter explicitly, bind new instrument/proof hashes, repeat both VQ arms and reject old receipts. Native baseline outputs can be retained because their instrument and weight convention are unaffected. Six contexts still cannot qualify a model even after the reference is repaired.

Commands and payload identities are included in each producer/supervisor record. The small audit script reads only the named BF16 normalization tensors from the already fully verified local artifacts, checking bounded extents and file stamps. It uses no model or GPU. A few top predictions prompted the investigation; no performance or held-out conclusion is drawn. Original source byte counts and SHA-256 values below precede replacement of the local home prefix with <HOME>. No tensor or logit binary is copied here. The exact files remain in the private research scratch directory.

### pr1788-norm-convention.json

````text
{"body":"## Requirements\n\n- ☑️ I understand it is strictly prohibited to use AI to write PR description\n- AI usage disclosure: the implementation in `mlx_lm/models/qwen4_exp.py` and the\n  unit test were written with Claude Code. Scope, design decisions and validation\n  are mine; I ran the full test suite and generation locally.\n\n## Model information\n\n- Name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next\n- Homepage: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next\n- Reference implementation: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp\n\n## Supported checkpoints\n\n- https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (official weights; converted 8-bit\n  group size 64 on the PR head, generated on an M3 Ultra 512 GB, ~600,000 tokens at\n  17-21 tok/s without crash or degradation)\n\nNote on convention (commit ac83bb4): the RMSNorm `+1` is folded into the weights\nduring sanitize, gated on the HF layout (raw keys carry the `model.language_model.`\nprefix; converted checkpoints read back as `model.*` and never re-trigger, so the\nfold cannot apply twice). `_FOLD_ONE` covers the eight non-gated norm suffixes\n(`linear_attn.norm` excluded, RMSNormGated scales by `w` alone). Conversions made\nfrom this PR's head before ac83bb4 carry normalized keys with unbaked norms: they\nload silently without the `+1` (no error, just degraded output) and must be redone.\n\nNote on `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit`: that quant bakes a `+1` into its\nnon-gated norm weights, which is exactly the convention this port has followed\nsince ac83bb4: the reference's `+1` is folded into the weights during sanitize and\nthe runtime applies the weight bare, so the quant loads correctly as-is and needs\nno repair. Subtracting 1.0 in memory is now harmful, it would remove a `1` the\nruntime no longer adds. The sanitize fold never touches this quant: it is gated on\nthe raw-HF `model.language_model.` prefix, and the quant carries the flat\n`language_model.` form. The Verification output below was produced with that quant\nbefore the convention fix.\n\n## Verification\n\nRun mlx-lm command:\n\n```console\nmlx_lm.generate --model Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit -p \"The secret to baking a good cake is\" -m 256\n```\n\nOutput:\n\n```\n==========\nWe need to respond to user: \"The secret to baking a good cake is\". They likely want\ncompletion? Need answer in English. Need final concise maybe helpful. Need maybe\ncomplete sentence. Could provide tips. Need ensure not too much? User fragment maybe\nasking to finish. We can answer: \"The secret to baking a good cake is...\" with key\nfactors: accurate measurements, room-temp ingredients, not overmixing, proper oven\ntemp, don't open door, test doneness. Need maybe if they want a single secret: balance\nof moisture and structure? Let's craft helpful completion.\n\u003c/think\u003e\nThe secret to baking a good cake is **precision and care**: measure ingredients\naccurately, use room-temperature butter/eggs when required, don't overmix the batter,\nand bake at the correct temperature without opening the oven too early.\n==========\nPrompt: 60 tokens, 1.457 tokens-per-sec\nGeneration: 171 tokens, 24.036 tokens-per-sec\nPeak memory: 111.020 GB\n```\n\nLeft padding and batched decoding: the QSA pooling grid is anchored on each row's first\nreal token instead of the buffer start, and the batched caches keep the indexer state\nacross `merge` (formula credited to Blaizzy/mlx-vlm#2028). Max |batch - row-by-row| on\nthe padded row, before and after:\n\n```\n                                     before      after\n  equal lengths (control)          4.47e-07    4.47e-07\n  padded, QSA on, attention only   6.54e-01    3.58e-07\n  padded, hybrid without PLE       6.17e-01    4.17e-07\n```\n\nEnd to end through `BatchGenerator` (prompts of 37/21/9, multi-chunk prefill) the\ngenerated tokens are identical to per-row `generate_step`; before the change the same\nrun crashed, the indexer restarting empty after `merge`.\n\nTwo padding bugs outside the QSA were fixed along the way: `conv_mask` was hardcoded to\n`None`, and the deltanet conv state, the PLE short-conv state and the n-gram context\ntail all read `[:, -n:]`, i.e. the padding of a right-padded row.\n\nStill wrong: a model fed an already left-padded `ids` tensor, where the n-gram hash and\n`_shift_right` read the padding tokens at the head (5.7e-01). That path is not reachable\nthrough mlx-lm's API, since `BatchGenerator` right-pads the prompt and only `finalize`\nturns it into left padding. `_AttnCache.to_quantized` also still drops `.indexer`, so QSA\ngoes silent under `--kv-bits`; pre-existing and unrelated to padding.\n\n## Reference output (if you have access to CUDA hardware)\n\nNot available - no CUDA hardware. The 180B checkpoint does not fit the reference\nimplementation on this machine (M3 Max, 128 GB).\n\nCross-checked against mlx-vlm's merged qwen4_exp (Blaizzy/mlx-vlm#2028): same\nzero-centered RMSNorm convention (`y * (1 + w)`, gated variant conventional), same\nper-query tail in the indexer (`tail_starts` from each query's complete-block count),\nsame row-sharded n-gram embedding. Their implementation additionally handles\nleft_padding for ragged batches, which this port now handles too (see below).\n\n\n\n\n","head":"2097324ed04ff76078366c77148b88b9db612ba2"}
````

### audit-vq-norms-v1.py

Original bytes: 2240. SHA-256: `4a8fb5d6e8f565d8e76be8d144b31c47562e716fd37235544ba676c4a82d85ff`.

````text
import hashlib,json,os,stat,struct
from pathlib import Path
ROOT=Path('.build/quantization-research')
SUFFIXES=('q_layernorm.weight','k_layernorm.weight','q_norm.weight','k_norm.weight','hc_norm.weight','norm_key.weight','norm_query.weight','norm_conv.weight')
def row(root,key,index):
 fd=os.open(root/index[key],os.O_RDONLY|os.O_NOFOLLOW|os.O_NONBLOCK)
 with os.fdopen(fd,'rb') as f:
  before=os.fstat(f.fileno());assert stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode)
  n=struct.unpack('<Q',f.read(8))[0];assert 0<n<4_000_000
  m=json.loads(f.read(n))[key];lo,hi=m['data_offsets'];assert m['dtype']=='BF16' and 0<hi-lo<=100_000 and hi+8+n<=before.st_size
  f.seek(8+n+lo);b=f.read(hi-lo);assert len(b)==hi-lo and os.fstat(f.fileno())==before
 return b
base=Path('<HOME>/.slotstream/models/qwen38-flash-next-mlx-4bit')
bi=json.loads((base/'model.safetensors.index.json').read_text())['weight_map']
result={'scope':'metadata and small-tensor diagnosis; no model forward','policy':'BF16 round-to-nearest-even of 1 + each non-gated norm; gated norm unchanged','artifacts':{}}
for arm in ['3.2','4.4']:
 root=ROOT/('candidate-'+arm);idx=json.loads((root/'model.safetensors.index.json').read_text())['weight_map']; records=[]
 for k in sorted(idx):
  if not k.startswith('model.') or not k.endswith(SUFFIXES):continue
  b=row(root,k,idx);baseline=row(base,'language_model.'+k,bi)
  v=[struct.unpack('<f',b'\0\0'+b[i:i+2])[0] for i in range(0,len(b),2)]
  folded=bytearray()
  for x in v:
   u=struct.unpack('<I',struct.pack('<f',1+x))[0];folded+=struct.pack('<H',(u+0x7fff+((u>>16)&1))>>16)
  records.append({'key':k,'bytes':len(b),'raw_sha256':hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest(),'folded_sha256':hashlib.sha256(folded).hexdigest(),'baseline_sha256':hashlib.sha256(baseline).hexdigest(),'raw_matches_baseline':b==baseline,'folded_matches_baseline':folded==baseline})
 result['artifacts'][arm]={'norms':len(records),'raw_matches':sum(r['raw_matches_baseline'] for r in records),'folded_matches':sum(r['folded_matches_baseline'] for r in records),'records':records}
(ROOT/'vq-norm-audit-v1.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps({k:{n:v[n] for n in ['norms','raw_matches','folded_matches']} for k,v in result['artifacts'].items()}))
````
